findings.issue_category: hard-coded AWS credentials in environment variables
findings.description: A static AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. They are committed to the repository, written to Terraform state, and readable by any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, creating a direct credential leak and lateral movement path.

findings.issue_category: environment variables not encrypted with CMK
findings.description: No kms_key_arn is set, so the environment variables - which here hold secret material - are protected only by the default AWS-managed key with no customer-managed key policy to constrain who can decrypt them; the values remain visible in plaintext to anyone who can describe the function.
The function targets the nodejs12.x runtime, which AWS has deprecated; it no longer receives security patches, leaving known unpatched vulnerabilities in the execution environment.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function executes outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or subnet-level egress control, easing exfiltration of data or the embedded credentials if the function is abused.
